-c5WEn18IeE.method: giving ChatGPT a scenario and having it generate a full set of test cases from it
-c5WEn18IeE.takeaway: How to turn a description of expected behaviour into structured test cases.

-k3TtT4iDks.method: ChatGPT's Study Mode (type /study), an interactive tutor that guides you with questions step by step instead of just handing over the answer
-k3TtT4iDks.takeaway: How to switch ChatGPT into tutor mode so it drills you on terms and ideas rather than doing the thinking for you.

-kLUwgtNn60.method: AI Academy's approach to long-form writing: never ask for the whole essay at once — break it into smaller prompts across two tabs and a document so you keep control of the argument
-kLUwgtNn60.takeaway: A workflow that automates the writing but not the thinking, so the argument stays yours and the draft stays checkable.

-quC5i44SsI.method: MacMost's copy-paste method — pull an article into reader view, paste it into ChatGPT after 'summarize this:', then ask for a set word count or a 10-bullet version; also how to grab a YouTube transcript to summarise a video
-quC5i44SsI.takeaway: How to compress a long reading or video into a summary of the exact length you need, and why pasting the source keeps it accurate.

6BJ0T8L7E5s.method: a back-and-forth mock interview with ChatGPT — it asks behavioural questions, you answer, and it critiques how you responded
6BJ0T8L7E5s.takeaway: A practice loop for interview answers, including feedback on structure and impact.

8Ct0rtFA2Hw.method: building a Custom GPT from scratch in ChatGPT and feeding it your own past writing so its output sounds like you rather than generic AI
8Ct0rtFA2Hw.takeaway: How to set up a reusable assistant with your instructions baked in, so you stop re-explaining context every session.

8qWtU51lxpM.method: dragging a dataset straight into ChatGPT and prompting it to describe the data, produce descriptive statistics per column, and chart the columns you care about
8qWtU51lxpM.takeaway: How to interrogate a spreadsheet conversationally, and why the 'analyzing' step means it ran real code rather than guessing.

A3WKdt_MNZQ.method: how retrieval-augmented generation works, then building a working RAG chatbot with Python, LangChain, Streamlit and a Pinecone vector database
A3WKdt_MNZQ.takeaway: The architecture behind a document-grounded chatbot, and a working build you can adapt.

ADUrUGQgksY.method: prompting ChatGPT to write Python (geopandas) that reads spatial files and plots them on a map, then running it in Google Colab
ADUrUGQgksY.takeaway: How to get working geospatial analysis code from a plain-English description of the map you want.

KcbXKUR7-a0.method: Gamma — turn a one-line prompt into a full slide deck, review the generated outline before it builds, then restyle with themes
KcbXKUR7-a0.takeaway: How to get a presentable deck out of a single prompt, editing the outline before any slides are made.

KzmGTTv6H6s.method: designing a study end-to-end in ChatGPT — research questions, hypotheses, survey items, sample size and sampling method, R code for the analysis, then implications and titles
KzmGTTv6H6s.takeaway: A full research-design workflow, including how to answer a reviewer who says your sample is too small.

LuHx6KdQPHQ.method: three brainstorming methods in ChatGPT — a reusable custom-instructions 'brainstorm paradigm', an AI-diagram tree that fans one topic into dozens of branches, and a SWOT prompt to pressure-test an idea
LuHx6KdQPHQ.takeaway: Three prompt patterns you can reuse to go from a blank page to a categorised list of options, plus a way to stress-test the one you pick.

M1n3xyKu5XA.method: uploading an image to ChatGPT with the + button and asking questions about it — the demo uploads a problem and asks ChatGPT to explain what it shows
M1n3xyKu5XA.takeaway: How to get AI to read a picture, diagram or screenshot you're stuck on, rather than trying to describe it in words.

NmVrXhbSJ2Y.method: drafting an email in ChatGPT and improving it through conversation — the first draft is deliberately generic, then detail is added turn by turn — plus what not to paste in for privacy
NmVrXhbSJ2Y.takeaway: Why the first draft always reads like AI, how to iterate it into your own voice, and to keep real names out of the prompt.

P9dEs3M_AA4.method: a 'teacher rubric' prompt that turns ChatGPT into a strict grader — paste your draft and the rubric, and it grades it and lists exactly what to fix before submission
P9dEs3M_AA4.takeaway: A prompt that gives you rubric-based feedback on a draft while you still have time to act on it.

RDVUioXNMIk.method: five prompts for practising spoken French with ChatGPT's voice mode, with a real roleplay demo in a workplace scenario
RDVUioXNMIk.takeaway: Concrete prompts for a spoken-French practice partner that corrects you as you go.

SDIrnL6nUkE.method: building a custom study plan with ChatGPT using the Ultralearning why/what/how framework — benchmarking how others learn it, then a week-by-week plan with deliverables and grading rubrics
SDIrnL6nUkE.takeaway: A prompt sequence that produces a personalised study schedule with checkable milestones, plus a pass where ChatGPT critiques the plan as an expert.

STJuR1zH8Ck.method: solving calculus problems in ChatGPT step by step, showing the working rather than just the final answer
STJuR1zH8Ck.takeaway: How to prompt for worked steps you can follow and verify, instead of a bare answer.

UWlzhXPUH68.method: prompting ChatGPT for a set of question-and-answer flashcards on a topic, then exporting the set straight into Quizlet
UWlzhXPUH68.takeaway: A pipeline from topic to a study-ready Quizlet deck in a couple of minutes.

W1YOYm9xdwA.method: pasting a broken snippet into ChatGPT with the prompt 'scan the following code for potential problems' — it finds the bug (a divide-by-zero), explains why it happens and returns a fixed version
W1YOYm9xdwA.takeaway: A debugging prompt formula, plus the habit of re-running the fixed code to confirm the error is actually gone.

WVAbJbO2CgI.method: ten ways to practise Spanish with AI, from conversation practice on the go through to correcting your own writing
WVAbJbO2CgI.takeaway: A set of Spanish-specific AI practice routines you can start using the same day.

_4-pggUACz0.method: prompts for refactoring legacy code with ChatGPT — restructuring for readability and modernising outdated syntax without changing what the code does
_4-pggUACz0.takeaway: Refactoring prompts that clean up messy code while preserving its behaviour.

du-_Ij4AXI0.method: using ChatGPT across the research-paper workflow — finding a topic where a genuine gap exists, then structuring the paper around it
du-_Ij4AXI0.takeaway: How to pick a defensible topic and lay out the sections before you start writing.

em39PxLmU-s.method: ResearchRabbit — seed it with one paper, then explore the citation network visually to surface related work and spot gaps
em39PxLmU-s.takeaway: A way to map a literature landscape from a single starting paper instead of searching keyword by keyword.

gI9kXjTl3ek.method: prompting ChatGPT for an annotated bibliography entry for a specific source, then checking it against APA, MLA or Chicago requirements
gI9kXjTl3ek.takeaway: How to draft summary-plus-evaluation annotations, and why you must verify every citation detail it produces.

in3BS4St3h0.method: using ChatGPT to build charts from data in minutes, then refining them and applying your own judgement to the story they tell
in3BS4St3h0.takeaway: How to get from raw numbers to a readable chart fast, and where human judgement still has to come in.

jPEknia0XNw.method: using ChatGPT for teaching prep — generating lesson plans, worksheets and classroom activities, then refining them module by module
jPEknia0XNw.takeaway: How to draft a lesson or unit quickly and then push ChatGPT for the objectives, activities and assessment.

kXeN0vkpshk.method: ChatGPT Projects as a workspace — turning a rough idea into a full plan with timelines, task assignments and a risk assessment that stays organised across sessions
kXeN0vkpshk.takeaway: How to go from a vague goal to a structured plan with milestones and risks, kept in one persistent workspace.

mim1TlFcX3g.method: three proofreading prompts run over the same document in ChatGPT — 'suggestions for improvement', 'proofread for clarity', then 'proofread for punctuation' — before editing in your own word processor
mim1TlFcX3g.takeaway: Three targeted passes that catch different problems, and the habit of applying the edits yourself rather than pasting output wholesale.

nBUl8Xz5MVY.method: a 10-step ChatGPT prompt system — standard definition, an explain-it-to-a-10-year-old version, real-life analogies, a simple diagram, then a comparison table — that you aim at any concept you're stuck on
nBUl8Xz5MVY.takeaway: A repeatable prompt sequence that turns a confusing idea into a definition, an analogy and a diagram you can check against your course notes.

r2JQTh8y3yk.method: Midjourney end to end — describe the image you want in plain language, get four variations back, then upscale and download the one you pick
r2JQTh8y3yk.takeaway: How to go from a written description to a usable generated image, and how upscaling changes the result.

rZvXeE5aZ3k.method: a timeline prompt for ChatGPT — paste your notes and ask for a clean chronology with date, event and why-it-matters columns, explicitly telling it not to invent facts and to flag anything uncertain
rZvXeE5aZ3k.takeaway: A prompt that turns messy notes into a sorted timeline, with a built-in guard against invented dates.

tIvzgSifYHM.method: a practice-exam prompt that specifies your course, the topic, how many questions, the format and the Bloom's-taxonomy level, plus an answer key — then asks for the rationale behind each answer
tIvzgSifYHM.takeaway: How to generate practice questions at the right difficulty and use the rationales to check your own reasoning.

uSVBfyHBiDU.method: Google NotebookLM — load PDFs, Drive docs, websites and YouTube videos as sources, then get summaries, ask questions answered only from those sources, and generate mind maps
uSVBfyHBiDU.takeaway: How to build a private research assistant grounded in your own documents rather than the open internet.

wa6SOJ87MhU.method: the fundamentals of ChatGPT — prompting basics, what it can and can't do, and how to personalise it
wa6SOJ87MhU.takeaway: Enough grounding to attempt an unfamiliar task with AI and judge whether the answer is trustworthy.

wvPxI_dm0d8.method: ChatGPT's Deep Research mode — it asks clarifying questions first, then spends minutes reading many sources and returns a long report with every claim linked to a citation
wvPxI_dm0d8.takeaway: How to commission a sourced research report, and where to open the activity log to see which sources it actually used.

xQXiSGDXknA.method: why open-ended chatting in your target language barely works, and how to use an LLM as one deliberate stage in a language-learning pipeline instead
xQXiSGDXknA.takeaway: A realistic picture of what AI can and can't do for language learning, and where it genuinely speeds you up.

xefUis03j_w.method: a compare-and-contrast prompt in ChatGPT (demonstrated on Buddhism vs Hinduism) that asks for similarities and differences, then expands any point you want more depth on
xefUis03j_w.takeaway: A prompt for structured comparisons, and how to push ChatGPT to elaborate on the specific dimension you care about.

promptPatterns.brainstorm: Give me 10 options grouped into 3 themes, then mark the 3 most original and explain what makes them stronger.
promptPatterns.citation:
For each source below write a 150-word annotation: what it argues, its method, and how it supports or complicates my argument. Use [APA / MLA / Chicago]. Then remind me to check every citation detail against the original — you can get these wrong.

[PASTE YOUR SOURCES HERE]
promptPatterns.code:
Tell me what's wrong, explain why it happens, then give the corrected version. Walk through the fixed code line by line with a concrete input.

[PASTE YOUR CODE AND THE ERROR HERE]
promptPatterns.compare: Give me a table of the key similarities and differences, then one short paragraph on which difference matters most and why.
promptPatterns.customgpt: Draft the name, description, instructions and 4 conversation starters for this Custom GPT. The instructions should tell it to ask clarifying questions and to admit when it doesn't know.
promptPatterns.data: I'm uploading my dataset. First describe what's in it and flag any data-quality problems, then answer my question, and show the code you ran so I can check it myself.
promptPatterns.dataviz: Recommend the best chart type for this data and say why, then produce it and explain what it does — and does not — show.
promptPatterns.email: Keep it under 150 words: polite, specific, with one clear ask. Give me two versions — one formal, one warmer. Don't include real names, ID numbers, or anything private.
promptPatterns.essay: Help me write this, don't write it for me. First ask me 3 questions about my argument, then propose a thesis and a section plan. Do not draft full paragraphs until I approve the plan.
promptPatterns.exam: Generate 15 practice questions — a mix of multiple choice and short answer, aimed at the 'apply' and 'analyse' levels. Include an answer key with the reasoning for each.
promptPatterns.explain: Start with a one-sentence definition, then explain it as if I'm 10, then give a real-world analogy. Finish by flagging anything scholars genuinely disagree about — and tell me what you're unsure of.
promptPatterns.feedback:
Act as a strict professor grading this. Score it against a rubric (argument, evidence, structure, style), give a letter grade, and list the 3 highest-impact fixes. Be blunt. Draft below:

[PASTE YOUR DRAFT HERE]
promptPatterns.flashcards: Create 20 flashcards formatted as 'Question | Answer', one per line, so I can paste them straight into Quizlet or Anki. Keep each answer under 25 words.
promptPatterns.general: Walk me through how to do this step by step. Ask me any clarifying questions first, and show your reasoning so I can check it.
promptPatterns.image: Give me 3 detailed image prompts, each specifying subject, style, lighting, composition and aspect ratio.
promptPatterns.interview: Act as the interviewer. Ask me one question at a time, wait for my answer, then critique it using the STAR structure and tell me exactly what to cut or add.
promptPatterns.language: Correct my mistakes, explain each correction briefly in English, then ask me a follow-up question to keep the conversation going.
promptPatterns.lessonplan: Give learning objectives, a timed activity sequence, the materials needed, and an assessment with a rubric.
promptPatterns.litreview:
Group the sources below into themes, show where they agree and disagree, and name the gap that's left. Do not invent sources.

[PASTE SOURCES OR ABSTRACTS HERE]
promptPatterns.notes: Answer using only the sources I upload, and cite which source each claim comes from. If my sources don't answer the question, say so instead of guessing.
promptPatterns.outline: Give a topic-sentence outline only — not full prose. For each section, state the argument it makes and the evidence it would need.
promptPatterns.projectplan: Break this into phases with milestones, working backwards from [DUE DATE]. Include the top 3 risks and how I'd mitigate each.
promptPatterns.proofread:
Do three passes: (1) clarity, (2) grammar and punctuation, (3) concision. Show every change as a list with a reason — don't silently rewrite. Text below:

[PASTE YOUR TEXT HERE]
promptPatterns.research: List credible sources with a one-line note on what each contributes. Prioritise peer-reviewed work, include links, and tell me explicitly if you are not certain a source exists.
promptPatterns.researchdesign: Propose a research question, hypotheses, method, sample and sampling strategy, and the analysis plan. Then critique the weaknesses of your own design.
promptPatterns.slides: Give me a slide-by-slide outline first (title plus 3 bullets each) and wait for my approval before expanding anything. Aim for [NUMBER] slides.
promptPatterns.studymode: Define each term in one clear sentence, then give a concrete example of each in context. Once I've read them, quiz me on them one at a time and tell me what I got wrong and why.
promptPatterns.studyplan: I have [X hours per week] and my exam is on [DATE]. Build a week-by-week plan with specific deliverables, and for each week give me a way to check I've actually learned it.
promptPatterns.summarize:
Give me (1) a three-sentence summary, (2) five bullet-point key claims, and (3) anything the author asserts without supporting evidence. Text below:

[PASTE THE TEXT HERE]
promptPatterns.timeline:
Turn this into a clean chronological timeline with columns for date, event, and why it matters (one sentence each). Do not invent dates — flag anything uncertain.

[PASTE YOUR NOTES HERE]
promptPatterns.vision: I'm uploading an image. Describe what you can actually see first, then interpret it, and tell me what you're uncertain about.
